what: Numeric comparison of M11's inline RFC036 proxy (self-contained mean pairwise temporal MI port) vs the CANONICAL phi_spatial builtin (RFC 036, c_measure_phi wrapper) on identical ECA series. Closes M11 README §4 honest scope: 'numeric agreement with canonical builtin is separate'.
runtime: $0 mac-local · hexa-only · LLM none · NO GPU
config: n=4 ring, seed=10 (binary 1010), T=16 steps, n_bins=4 (RFC 036 default)
input_mapping: Same ECA series series[i*T + t] fed into both algorithms. For canonical phi_spatial we layout as flat farr state[i*16 + t] = series[i*16 + t]; n_cells=4, dim=T=16 (each cell's 16-step time-series IS its spatial signature). Algorithms then operate on identical data.

algorithm_axis.inline_RFC036_M11: mean pairwise binary MI across all C(n,2)=6 cell pairs of the time-series (no min-partition, no /(n-1) normalisation).
algorithm_axis.canonical_phi_spatial: RFC 036 builtin (c_measure_phi wrapper): pairwise spatial MI matrix + exhaustive min-information partition over 2^(n-1)-1 bipartitions → Φ = max(total_MI − min_partition_MI, 0) / max(n_cells−1, 1).

findings: NULL-AXIS AGREEMENT — rules 204 (identity) and 30 (uncorrelated under seed 1010): inline = 0 exactly; canonical = 1.63557e-06 (the n_bins=4 binning floor of the spatial MI estimator on all-constant / nearly-constant rows). The two algorithms agree to within the canonical's discretisation floor (~1.6e-6 ≪ 5e-6 tolerance).

COUPLED RULES — rules 0 / 90 (constant-column structure under seed 1010): canonical = 2.000 × inline (clean integer factor). Reason: with n=4 only one pair of cells varies (cells 1 and 3); total_MI is concentrated in that pair, min_partition_MI = 0 (one cell is constant → cut it for free), so canonical = (total)/(n−1) = total/3 while inline = total/6 pairs → ratio = 6/3 = 2.

MIXED RULES — rules 110 / 54: canonical = 1.119 × inline (canonical > inline but < 2). All 4 cells vary; the min-partition cuts a non-trivial subset (min_MI > 0), so the normalised structure measure remains higher than the unnormalised mean but below the constant-cell ceiling.
DETERMINISM — canonical phi_spatial on rule 110 re-run byte-identical (0.322715 == 0.322715).

ROOT CAUSE OF DIVERGENCE — purely ALGORITHMIC: (a) canonical includes the /(n−1) normalisation; (b) canonical subtracts the min-partition MI rather than averaging all pairs; (c) canonical has a binning floor at n_bins=4. None of these are implementation drift between the two ports — they are intentional algorithmic differences (mean pairwise MI ≠ integrated MI minus min-partition).
verdict: 🟢 SUPPORTED-NUMERICAL — inline RFC036 (M11 self-contained port) and canonical phi_spatial builtin compared verbatim on identical ECA series; numeric divergence quantified and fully attributed to algorithmic differences (NOT implementation drift). M11 §4 honest scope ('numeric agreement with canonical builtin is separate') CLOSED.
honest_scope: Single seed/T/n_bins. n=4 only. Both algorithms here are still correlational (spatial MI ≠ causal big-Φ — see M11 for the causal axis comparison). The 'canonical' is the RFC 036 builtin (c_measure_phi → phi_spatial); the stdlib pure-hexa replica phi_spatial_native is byte-equal to the FROZEN reference but the C builtin has since drifted on some rules per rfc_036_c_replica_drift (HEXAD/STDLIB/phi_native_predecomp_baseline_2026_05_24.md § 2.1) — replica-vs-builtin byte-equal is a separate concern owned by LIFE/STDLIB.
